sweep_summary: Wandala (wand1278) is not in the catalog. All three keyword items Glottolog attaches to it (Liu & Takeda 2021; Broselow, Park & Archibald 1995; Haraguchi 1996) are 'mora'-trigger mislinks (Mora = the Cameroonian town where Wandala is spoken): they treat English rhythm classes, L2 prosody, and Japanese accent respectively, confirmed from Crossref records/abstract and Google Books snippets (files under, listed). Priority none for all three. No first-hand Wandala stress statement was read: the named decider remains Frajzyngier 2012, A Grammar of Wandala, ch. 2 Phonology pp. 24-76 (De Gruyter, doi 10.1515/9783110218411. controls, DNB TOC d-nb.info/1120544904/34 403, the Internet Archive landing page gives only the chapter list, Unpaywall closed per earlier reading). Available secondary evidence is tone-only: the publisher blurb and Wikipedia (two tones, three vowels), Frajzyngier 2020 OH chapter abstract (two tones), Schuh 2017 family-level 'no Chadic language has stress as a prosodic parameter'. Google Books snippets that pair 'Wandala' with 'stress' are about other languages (Wolff 2006 'Stress is marginally contrastive and occurs only in the subgrammar of nouns' = Lamang; OHLP snippet = Somali/Hetzron). Other candidate primary sources remain print/walled: Fluckiger & Whaley 1981a (SIL Yaounde; sil.org 403), Mirt 1969 ZDMG Suppl. I (Halle repository behind Anubis bot wall), Eguchi 1969b KUAS 3 (Kyoto repository JS shell), Loehr 2002b Malgwa grammar (Peter Lang; Frankfurt repository bot wall), Wolff & Naumann 2004 (Brill). Acquisition priority for a future pass: high for Frajzyngier 2012 ch. 2 (library copy; one prosody subsection page would decide), medium for Loehr 2002b and Fluckiger & Whaley 1981a. OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs could not be reached by automated download.

tone_statements.citation: Made Boukar. 2023. Le wandala – tchadique central – en contact avec le fulfulde au nord du Cameroun. Revue DELLA/Afrique (ACAREF), vol. 5, n° spécial – décembre 2023, Tome 1 (Lettres, langues, arts, éducation, enseignement, pédagogie, didactique), pp. 237-252. [online 4 January 2024; no DOI]
tone_statements.quote: Pour ce qui est du système consonantique, le fulfulde n’a pas de labio-vélaires (kw, gw, ngw) ni de latérales fricatives (ɬ, ɮ). Le wandala, quant à lui est dépourvu de nasale palatale (ny). Le fulfulde est une langue sans tons, alors que le wandala en registre deux tonals (haut et bas).
tone_statements.translation: As for the consonant system, Fulfulde has no labio-velars (kw, gw, ngw) nor lateral fricatives (ɬ, ɮ). Wandala, for its part, lacks the palatal nasal (ny). Fulfulde is a language without tones, whereas Wandala registers two tones [sic: 'deux tonals'] (high and low).
tone_statements.locator: p. 243, section 3 'La comparaison des deux systèmes consonantique et vocalique (wandala/fulfulde)'
tone_statements.summary: 2 tones: H, L (secondary statement, after Frajzyngier).

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2017. A Chadic Cornucopia, ed. Paul Newman. Oakland: eScholarship, California Digital Library.
sources.note: Family level only, no Wandala-specific statement: ch. 5 'All Chadic languages are tone languages.. Stress as distinctive prosodic property has been discussed in Hunter (1980) for Hausa and Wolff (1983, 2015b) for Lamang (and perhaps in a few other Chadic language studies), but prosodic amplitude in Chadic phonological systems generally is a function of the interaction of tone, syllable weight, and intonation and plays no role that is not attributable to those properties.' Book outline p. 6: 'stress: no Chadic language has stress as a prosodic parameter'. Mandara mentioned only for pluractiona…

sources.note: scanned text only. The Wandala chapter (§1 Orthographie: confusion of related sounds, abundance of guttural/lingual sounds; roots; comparison) carries no Wandala-specific accent/stress statement. The general introduction only says the author marks accents consistently in all his vocabularies ('durch eine durchgeführte Accentuirung', scanned l. 1643) so that a European pronouncing the words is understood; no rule of placement is stated.

sources.citation: Wolff, H. Ekkehard. 2025. Typology and evolution of minimal vowel systems in Central Chadic. Ch. 7 in Kuznetsova et al. (eds.), [Language Science Press book 415]. Berlin: LangSci.
sources.note: Discusses the Mandara (Wandala) vowel system (Mirt 1969, Fluckiger & Whaley 1981, Wolff & Naumann 2004; fn. 23: Frajzyngier 2012 posits /a, i, u/ plus epenthetic vowel and harmony). Nothing on Wandala stress; only the general remark (p. 263) that schwa cannot carry stress but can carry tone.

sources.note: Contact/loanword study (Wandala-Fulfulde) with a short structuralist phonology section (consonant table after Frajzyngier, vowel tables) and one comparative tone statement: Fulfulde has no tones whereas Wandala has two tones, high and low (sentence is printed garbled: 'en registre deux tonals'). Tone-marked Wandala loan forms (e.g. bàba, dʒàɓamà, gùdèl) are given; no discussion of tone rules, TBU, downstep or grammatical tone; nothing on stress/accent.
